item.title: Big Ten bans NFL returnees, putting LSU and Lane Kiffin on collision course with the SEC
item.description: Big Ten's new rule bars players with NFL experience from eligibility as lawsuits and injunctions reshape the college football transfer landscape.
item.content:encoded:
The Big Ten has taken steps to prevent athletes who have signed NFL contracts from joining the conference this season — and in the future.

Following recent developments that have seen former college players enter the professional ranks, only to regain college eligibility through court orders, the conference voted Tuesday to bar those athletes moving forward.

Under the new Big Ten policy, any athlete who has signed with a professional team, declared for the NFL Draft or participated in any type of professional training camp will be ineligible for conference competition.

NFL TO NCAA? COURTROOM CHAOS IS GIVING PRO ATHLETES A BIZARRE PATH BACK TO COLLEGE, AND IT'S ONLY JUST BEGUN

The decision comes after players in several states were granted injunctions or temporary restraining orders allowing them to play this season.

Most of the lawsuits stem from the NCAA’s new eligibility guidelines, which give athletes five years to play five seasons of college athletics.

Since June, there have been a plethora of lawsuits filed in state courts that have granted athletes an additional season of eligibility, with multiple judges ruling in favor of plaintiffs that argued the NCAA's new rules should have included them being grandfathered into the process.

In recent days, LSU head coach Lane Kiffin has taken a beating in the court of public opinion, and from many within the SEC, for bringing back players who have already gained NFL experience.

This includes former Ole Miss football players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, who are both set to join the LSU roster thanks to a ruling from the 19th District Court of Louisiana that granted them an additional season of eligibility.

LSU’S LANE KIFFIN FIRES BACK AT NFL RETURNEE BACKLASH: BLAME THE NCAA, NOT US FOR RECRUITING PRO ATHLETES

But, there have been plenty others who have gone down this route, winning cases in state courts that allow them to return this season. Texas offensive lineman Cole Hutson is another, who sued the NCAA in a Texas court for an additional season.

In the SEC, there are meetings taking place over the next 24 hours that include Presidents, Chancellors and athletic directors. They are discussing their path forward, with a number of them in favor of the conference implementing the same rule as the Big Ten.

OREGON COACH DAN LANNING LAYS OUT MULTIPLE REASONS WHY NFL PLAYERS RETURNING TO COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS 'UNFAIR'

The problem is that LSU sees its own way around the conference ruling, thanks to a Louisiana court order.

If the conference were to start governing themselves more than normal, we could end up seeing a school like LSU testing the legal strength of a court order, by including the SEC in a lawsuit against the NCAA.

Officials from LSU will be in Birmingham, Alabama with their colleagues this week discussing the ongoing situation. A majority of SEC officials are against the idea of athletes with NFL experience returning to college, according to sources.

While the Tigers could back off their stance to take athletes from the NFL, head coach Lane Kiffin has essentially put his foot in the ground when it comes to this disagreement.

"So, you know, we have you know made a decision to recruit some kids around the country, and through these multiple injunctions around the country, which, this is not a first time in college sports, a group of players were granted a fifth year of eligibility, in multiple sports. And through them winning their injunction and entry into the portal, they’re available to recruit," Kiffin noted on Monday.

"So ourselves, like many places around the country, are recruiting them. At the end of the day, you know, because of these rulings, they’re either going to play for you or they’re going to play somewhere else around the country. So, we made a decision to recruit them, like probably most people are."

Will this turn into a legal battle within the SEC?

Sure, it could, if the Tigers administration feels as though it could win the court battle that could be lying ahead with its own conference.

There are plenty of SEC officials who would like to see the conference go the same route as the Big Ten, with the ACC and Big 12 discussing their own path forward with a new rule.

Time will tell, but there seems to be a battle brewing in the Bayou.

And, it could involve a team deciding it is prepared to battle its own conference over a new rule.

item.title: Triathlete channels his inner 'Three Stooges' to escape harrowing alligator attack in South Carolina
item.description: Jonathan Bruney fought off a large alligator attack in South Carolina's Savannah River by gouging its eye during Ironman triathlon training.
item.content:encoded:
A triathlete got more than he bargained for when he went for a swim in a local South Carolina river in preparation for an Ironman competition next month.

Jonathan Bruney, 31, was training for an upcoming triathlon in the Savannah River on Sunday when he felt an unfamiliar but powerful pain in his arm.

"Out of nowhere, it hit me," Bruney told CBS affiliate WRDW. "It was a pretty big impact to my right side… it felt as if my elbow had made a hard impact, maybe like diving on a gym basketball court."

SON OF FLORIDA ALLIGATOR ATTACK VICTIM SAYS TOURISTS AND TIKTOKERS ARE EMBOLDENING THE GATORS

Bruney said he was swimming when he thought he hit a log at first, before pain started shooting up his entire arm confirming that something far more serious was afoot.

A large alligator had latched onto Bruney's right arm, and the endurance athlete suddenly went into survival mode.

"I immediately thought, ‘I need to get this off of me,’ because I didn’t want him to spin or death roll and do even more damage," Bruney explained.

Rather than panic, Bruney remembered a weak spot and acted almost instinctively.

SHARK WEEK PUTS SHARK BITE SURVIVAL IN FOCUS WITH ER DOC'S EXPERT TIPS

"I just knew the eyes were what you should target," Bruney said. "I put my hand on the snout, reached up, and pushed my thumb into his eyeball, and he released."

After he emerged from the water, Bruney was bleeding so profusely that a fellow triathlete (and first responder), Matthew Davis, had to use a cord from his swim buoy as a makeshift tourniquet, WRDW reported.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

After a bystander called 911, first responders were able to get Bruney to a local hospital, where doctors were able to determine that the injuries were treatable and not long-term in nature.

"It could have been a lot worse," Bruney told the outlet.

He added that although he doesn't fear the water after the incident, he now has a "healthy respect" for it, and still plans to compete in the Ironman triathlon next month.

item.title: Michigan Democrat awkwardly pivots to circumcision during heated Fox News debate on child sex changes
item.description: Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed deflected questions on sex changes for minors, comparing the issue to circumcision.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Dr. Abdul El-Sayed addressed questions about sex changes for minors and transgender athletes in women’s sports during a tense exchange on Fox News Monday night.

Speaking on "Jesse Watters Primetime," the progressive candidate and former Detroit Health Department director initially avoided giving direct answers on the issues.

"Sex changes for minors. Do you support that?" asked host Jesse Watters Monday.

HHS OFFICIAL WARNS OF IRREVERSIBLE RISKS AS TRUMP ADMIN RESTRICTS FUNDING FOR YOUTH GENDER PROCEDURES

El-Sayed referenced "great conversations" about right-to-try legislation and said he believes the government should not limit the healthcare a person is allowed to receive.

"I just think the government shouldn't tell you what kind of healthcare you should have and if you're a minor, it's between you and your doctor and your parents," El-Sayed said.

FTC ALLEGES INFLUENTIAL TRANSGENDER HEALTH ORGANIZATION MISLED PARENTS ABOUT SAFETY OF YOUTH TREATMENTS

"If you disagree that healthcare decisions need to be made by a doctor, their parents and a patient, then I just think we agree to disagree. But you know, you want to put government inside a clinic or a hospital selectively," he added.

Watters then asked El-Sayed if he supported cutting off the genitalia of minors. El-Sayed responded by raising circumcision as another example involving parental consent in medical care for children, asking Watters if he himself is circumcised.

"I mean, so do you really want to have this conversation? Are you circumcised?" El-Sayed asked.

"I think it’s a problem that you think that you get to decide what happens between a parent, a doctor and a patient. And I'm just saying that, yes, circumcision is surgery on a kid's ding-a-ling. So if you really want to bring that up, you can. I just think you guys are really selective about how you want to talk about these things," he later added.

ABDUL EL-SAYED’S MEDICARE-FOR-ALL CRUSADE COLLIDES WITH AN AWKWARD CONTRADICTION INVOLVING HIS WIFE

"Abdul, Michigan's not going for that. That is sick stuff," Watters responded before moving the conversation toward transgender athletes in women’s sports.

El-Sayed initially declined to answer the question, instead saying Watters had not asked about issues "people actually care about in Michigan," including groceries and healthcare.

"You don’t seem to want to talk about any of those things. You want to bring up all this culture war that, you know, I'm not here to fight a culture war, I’m here to fight the affordability crisis that people are facing," he added.

The pair later returned to transgender athletes in women’s sports, with El-Sayed saying the rules should be "decided by the people who govern sports."

REPUBLICANS GET THE DEMOCRAT THEY WANTED AS SOCIALIST ABDUL EL-SAYED WINS MICHIGAN SENATE PRIMARY

The tense exchange was part of a wide-ranging segment in which Watters and El-Sayed also went back and forth on wealth taxes, religious freedom and foreign policy, while El-Sayed repeatedly tried to shift focus to working-class economic concerns.

El-Sayed is the Democratic nominee for Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat and is set to face Republican nominee Mike Rogers in November. He earned a doctorate in public health from Oxford University and a medical degree from Columbia University.

item.title: Taylor Fritz is dating Olivia Jade, Sunday Ticket is highway robbery & Dolly Parton's best sports moments
item.description: Taylor Fritz steps out with Olivia Jade, Sunday Ticket continues to gouge NFL fans and a look back on Dolly Parton's iconic Cowboys halftime show.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

I'm not a person who gets starstruck.

Maybe it's the line of work I'm in. Since college, I've spent my entire career working with professional athletes, including some of the biggest names in MLB and the NFL. And working in sports, I've crossed paths with countless other celebrities, too — actors, musicians, TV personalities.

I don't say that as some sort of not-so-humble brag. It's just a fact that even the biggest stars on the planet are still people, and none of them have ever really blown me away in real life.

Except one: Dolly Parton.

Back in 2016, devastating wildfires ripped through Gatlinburg, Tenn., burning more than 17,900 acres, damaging or destroying roughly 2,400 structures and killing 14 people.

In addition to donating her own money, Dolly established the My People Fund, which ultimately provided millions of dollars directly to families who lost their homes in the disaster. I ran social media for the Titans at the time, and a few of our players volunteered to answer phones during Dolly's telethon to help raise money for the victims.

I'll never forget walking into that studio and immediately being greeted by the blondest, biggest hair and the sparkliest rhinestones I'd ever seen.

"Thanks for coming," she said with a huge smile. "I'm Dolly!"

Folks, I could not breathe.

I could not believe this living legend was standing right in front of me, reaching out to shake my hand. How could someone so tiny be so... larger than life?

They say never to meet your heroes, but that wasn't true with Dolly. She couldn't have been kinder or more genuine. Everything I imagined her to be.

And the wildfire relief was just the tip of the iceberg for a woman who seemed to pour everything she had into the people and places she cared about.

Through the Dollywood Foundation, she created Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, which has mailed hundreds of millions of free books to young children around the world. She funded scholarships for local students, helped provide tuition assistance for Dollywood employees and donated millions of dollars to medical research at Vanderbilt University Medical Center.

That generosity wasn't some side project attached to her celebrity. It was part of who she was.

In the video announcing her death Tuesday, Dolly's nephew Bryan Seaver said, "She never saw a door she couldn't open, and the doors she opened made and changed history."

We can learn a lot from Dolly — how to treat our fellow human beings, how to show up for our communities and how to be so unapologetically true to ourselves that we don't give a damn what anyone has to say about it.

Dolly's music will live forever. But her legacy is so much bigger than the songs.

It's in the kids who learned to love reading because a book showed up in their mailbox. It's in the families who had somewhere to turn after losing everything. It's in the people she helped simply because she could.

And, selfishly, it'll always be in the memory of one dumbstruck 27-year-old standing in a television studio, temporarily forgetting how to breathe because Dolly Parton smiled, reached out her hand and said, "I'm Dolly."

What a gift she was.

We've made it, folks — the weekend you've all been waiting for.

You've had it in your calendars all year, you've sat around all summer desperately yearning for it to get here, counting the days and weeks as they slowly ticked by. And finally it's here.

The Bassmaster Elite at St. Lawrence River.

You thought I was going to say college football, didn't you? Well that, too! After a summer full of nauseating WNBA drama, that UNC-TCU kickoff in Dublin is gonna hit like crack. (As they say. I've never tried it.)

But I am very pumped about this fishing tournament, too. You may have noticed — as a part of our spiffy new rebrand — OutKick OutDoors is now an official arm of our website. And the St. Lawrence will be our first major event.

RANDY MOSS LAUNCHES YOUTUBE BASS FISHING SERIES WHILE HEADLINING RECORD $3.25M TOURNAMENT IN NASHVILLE

After the tournament, we'll be in a boat for the Randy Moss Pro-Am, where a bunch of Pro Football Hall of Famers will take on the top bass anglers in the country. It's going to be a hoot.

So make sure you're following us on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, and don't miss out, OK?!

Now that we have that out of the way, it's time to see what the internet is up to today. Grab your favorite cold beverage and settle in for your Tuesday 'Cap.

Look, I know Bobby wrote about this yesterday and it was a hot topic in our newsletter this morning. But I just cannot get over how expensive NFL Sunday Ticket is these days. $480! And for what?

I've had Sunday Ticket for years. I'm a Miami Dolphins fan (womp, womp), and — aside from illegal streams that would almost certainly fill my laptop with viruses — Sunday Ticket used to be the only way I could watch every Phins snap from my house in Middle Tennessee.

But this year, my husband and I had pretty much decided we weren't going to renew it.

So imagine our surprise when that $480 renewal fee hit the ol' bank account in EARLY JULY. YouTubeTV pulled a fast one, alright — slapping us with the auto-renewal a full two months before the season even starts.

Dirty.

So here I am again. Paying damn near $500 to watch my crappy football team play crappy football.

At least I won't have to deal with this dude anymore.

This sort of stuff was endearing when we were putting up 70 points on the Broncos. It got really old after Tua's 37th concussion.

Oh well, your problem now, Justin Herbert.

Who is Olivia Jade?

Thank you for asking. Olivia Jade is an influencer (because that's a job in the Year of our Lord 2026), but she's also Lori Loughlin's daughter.

Aunt Becky Jr., if you will.

She looks just like her, too.

The daughter who went to USC thanks to that big college admissions scandal?!

That very same one.

Anyway, she's bounced back and is now dating tennis star Taylor Fritz. But reps say they're just "taking things slow." Whatever that means in celebrity-speak.

Listen, summer is winding down (don't tell Joe Kinsey I said that), and love is in the air. We've got all these NFL WAGs petting their husbands and boyfriends at training camp. We've got golfer Wyndham Clark and Emily Tanner moving in together. We've got Bryson DeChambeau hard launching with Mikayla Demaiter.

And now Taylor and Olivia.

Cuffing season is right around the corner, single folks. Get on it.

No mailbag or funny dog videos this time, kids.

I think the only appropriate way to end our Nightcaps today is by honoring the Queen of Tennessee herself.

Fly high, Dolly. There'll never be another one like you.

item.title: Trump mourns Dolly Parton, orders US flags lowered nationwide after country music icon dies
item.description: Trump ordered American flags lowered nationwide for one week in honor of Dolly Parton, calling her death "a true loss for millions of people."
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump ordered American flags lowered across the United States for one week Tuesday, as he mourned the death of country music icon Dolly Parton, telling the legendary singer, "The World loves you."

Parton died peacefully Tuesday in Nashville, Tennessee, according to an announcement shared by her representatives. She was 80.

"Very sad to report that Dolly Parton, one of the greatest Country singers, and far beyond, EVER, has just passed away," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "This is a true loss for millions of people. There has never been anyone like her, and never will."

DOLLY PARTON’S ONGOING HEALTH BATTLE FORCES COUNTRY LEGEND TO MISS MAJOR DOLLYWOOD EVENT

Trump then announced a presidential tribute to Parton.

"In her honor, I am lowering the American flag throughout the United States for a one week period beginning tonight at 6:00PM," Trump wrote. "Rest in Peace, Dolly! The World loves you."

Trump's tribute came as Parton's family and representatives remembered a woman whose influence stretched far beyond the country music stages that made her famous.

"A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family," the announcement said. "Dolly Parton’s legacy is one of love, compassion, and resilience."

DOLLY PARTON CANCELS LAS VEGAS RESIDENCY AS HEALTH ISSUES FORCE HER TO STEP BACK FROM STAGE PERFORMANCES

Parton, born Jan. 19, 1946, had a seven-decade career spanning music, songwriting, acting, writing and philanthropy.

She was preceded in death by her husband of 59 years, Carl Thomas Dean, who died in 2025, as well as her mother, Avie Lee Caroline Owens, and father, Robert Lee Parton Sr., according to the announcement.

DOLLY PARTON'S CALIFORNIA RETREAT WITH WIG ROOM AND DOLLYWOOD BIRDHOUSE LISTS FOR $1.95M

At Parton's request, a small, private service will be held for immediate family. Fans and friends were encouraged to pay tribute on social media or through Parton's official website.

In lieu of flowers, the family asked for donations to Dolly Parton's Imagination Library.

TAYLOR SWIFT'S VIDEO TRIBUTE TO ALAN JACKSON DIVIDES CROWD AT COUNTRY LEGEND'S FINAL SHOW

Parton's nephew and head of security, Bryan Seaver, also shared a video message following her death.

Tributes quickly poured in from Tennessee and across the country.

CARRIE UNDERWOOD, GARY SINISE LEAD STARS WHO'VE SHARED WHY THEY'RE PROUD TO BE AMERICANS

"There are no words to adequately express the sorrow our family and indeed, all Tennesseans, feel in the loss of Dolly Parton," Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., wrote on X. "An iconic leader who loved our great state and nation. Her passing leaves a void that no one can ever fill. Dolly, we will always love you."

House Republicans called Parton "an American icon" and "a national treasure," praising her as "a legendary artist, a generous philanthropist, and a proud daughter of Tennessee whose music and spirit touched generations of Americans."

SEN. LINDSEY GRAHAM DEAD AT 71 AFTER 'BRIEF AND SUDDEN' ILLNESS, OFFICE SAYS

Rep. Tim Burchett, R-Tenn., remembered Parton as "an incredible East Tennessean" who "never changed her accent or forgot where she came from."

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott announced his state would also lower its flags in Parton's honor.

"So sad to lose this legend," Abbott wrote on X. "Texas will lower our flags in her honor. God Bless Dolly."

House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., said "America has lost a true national treasure," pointing to Parton's Tennessee roots, worldwide success and philanthropy.

"Dolly Parton’s unmistakable voice, joyful spirit, and remarkable generosity touched generations of Americans and many others around the world," Johnson wrote. "From the mountains of Tennessee to stages across the globe, she never forgot where she came from, and she used her extraordinary success to lift up countless others."

The Department of the Interior paid tribute to Parton's deep connection to her Tennessee roots and the Great Smoky Mountains.

"Dolly Parton carried the music, stories and spirit of her Tennessee mountain home wherever she went," the department said. "She was a lifelong champion of the Great Smoky Mountains and proudly shared her love for them with the world."

The Franklin Police Department also mourned the singer, saying her "roots and heart were always deeply connected to Tennessee."

Parton's family said the music and generosity that defined her extraordinary life would endure.

"Her songs will continue to resonate with people of all ages," the announcement said, "and her philanthropic work will have a lasting impact."

item.title: Hayden Panettiere’s rep slams ‘gossip and speculation’ as death investigation deepens
item.description: The DEA is investigating Hayden Panettiere's death as her team says key details have yet to emerge and urges people with information to contact police.
item.content:encoded:
Hayden Panettiere’s team slammed the "gossip and speculation" that erupted after her shocking death and warned that the public still didn’t know the full story as investigators searched for answers.

Her representative condemned the speculation surrounding Panettiere’s final hours and accused outsiders of turning her death into fodder for gossip.

"Many people who were not close to Hayden are using her death as an opportunity to fuel gossip and speculation about a situation they knew very little about," Panettiere's rep said in a statement shared with US Weekly. "It is deeply disrespectful to her memory and to those who knew and loved her and are actively grieving this tremendous loss."

HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S BOYFRIEND’S BROTHER REVEALS WHAT HAPPENED INSIDE AIRBNB BEFORE ACTRESS'S DEATH

As the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) joined the investigation into Panettiere's death, her rep urged anyone with information to come forward.

"If you have legitimate information that could be helpful, please contact law enforcement rather than turning to social media to speculate publicly about something you do not fully understand."

POLICE SHOW UP AT HOME LINKED TO HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S ON-AND-OFF BOYFRIEND DAYS AFTER HER SUDDEN DEATH

Panettiere's team also hinted that key details surrounding Panettiere’s death had yet to emerge.

"There is much more to this story than what is currently being discussed publicly, and those closest to Hayden are actively cooperating with the ongoing investigation to help ensure that the truth comes to light and that justice is properly served," the statement concluded.

Fox News Digital reached out to Panettiere's representative for comment.

Panettiere died Aug. 16 at a South Carolina apartment. Preliminary autopsy results found no signs of trauma that contributed to Panettiere’s death, the Greenville County Coroner's Office confirmed to Fox News Digital. However, Panettiere's death remains under investigation.

Brian Hickerson, who had an on-again, off-again relationship with Panettiere in the years before her death at 36, was among those at the residence when she was found unresponsive, according to the police report obtained by Fox News Digital.

His presence there marked a striking final chapter in a relationship that had previously led to domestic violence charges and his eventual conviction.

Hickerson and his brother had called 911 after finding Panettiere unresponsive, according to the report. Authorities spoke to both Hickerson and his brother, Zach, and executed a search warrant at the home.

The police report claimed Zach appeared "very emotional" while paramedics worked to revive Panettiere. Meanwhile, Hickerson did not become emotional until the "Ice Princess" star was declared deceased.

Officers were also given a bag of medication Panettiere had allegedly been taking by Hickerson.

Hickerson reportedly traveled with the "Remember the Titans" actress from Los Angeles the day before she was found unresponsive at a Greenville, South Carolina, apartment complex on Aug. 16, according to TMZ. The two broke up briefly in 2022, but rekindled their romance the following year. Hickerson's brother confirmed to police Brian was in a relationship with the actress at the time of Panettiere's death.

item.title: Pritzker’s swagger stunt backfires as critics roast viral video: ‘Cringiest thing he’s ever posted’
item.description: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker's black-and-white "aura-farming" video drew widespread mockery on social media, with critics targeting his weight and taxes.
item.content:encoded:
Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker showed off his swagger in a tongue-in-cheek social media video Monday, prompting a wave of mockery from critics online.

The video, recorded in black and white and notching more than 1 million views, features Pritzker making a variety of model-like expressions at the camera behind a caption that reads "when you’re in an aura-farming contest and your opponent in JB." Aura-farming is a common piece of slang used to describe the taking of certain actions with the explicit goal of acquiring swag.

Many social media users did not agree with Pritzker’s assessment of himself.

PROGRESSIVE MINNEAPOLIS MAYOR'S VIRAL HIP-HOP MOVES SPARK 'HUMILIATION RITUAL' MOCKERY ONLINE

"Only thing bigger than the ratio this tweet is getting is…well," White House deputy assistant to the president Kaelan Dorr posted in response to the video.

"Pritzker is kind of a medical marvel," conservative commentator Matt Walsh wrote. "He looks gaunt and frail from Ozempic and also still morbidly obese at the exact same time. He's taking the concept of ‘skinny fat’ to places never thought possible."

WHITE HOUSE FIRES BACK AFTER 'SLOB' JB PRITZKER SAYS TRUMP IS SUFFERING FROM 'DEMENTIA'

Pritzker wrote the phrase "governor-maxxing" alongside his video on X. "Maxxing" as a suffix denotes that someone is doing something in a highly optimized way. "Looks-maxxing," for instance, refers to the act of taking one's appearance, physical fitness, and demeanor seriously as to maximize attractiveness.

Some on social media used the governor’s phrasing to poke fun at him.

Brian Costin, who is a high-level staffer at a right-of-center advocacy group in Illinois, accused Pritzker of "property-tax-maxxing," "state-and-local-tax-burden-maxxing," "cell-phone-tax-maxxing," "gas-tax-hike-maxxing," and "blaming-everyone-else-maxxing," among other things.

Others focused on his weight, claiming that Pritzker was "buffet-maxxing" or "waistline-maxxing."

REPUBLICANS RIP 4 BLUE STATES FOR KEEPING TAXES ON TIPS, OVERTIME AFTER TRUMP REPRIEVE

Pritzker has a history of making widely mocked social media posts, including his frequent attempts to spar with the president.

"Might be the cringiest thing he's ever posted, and that is saying a lot," RealClearPolitics president Tom Bevan wrote.

Pritzker's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: El-Sayed's defense of Sharia law stance sparks online eruption from Christians, conservatives: 'He's done'
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's comparison of Sharia law to Catholic canon law during his Jesse Watters interview ignited fierce pushback from conservative commentators.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed sparked controversy on social media Monday night after comparing Sharia law to Christian canon law during an interview with Fox News anchor Jesse Watters.

"Getting rid of Sharia law is White supremacy?" Watters said to El-Sayed, bringing up past comments from the Michigan candidate opposing a ban on Sharia law and comparing those efforts to White supremacy. "Can you explain that one?"

Sayed responded by comparing Sharia, Islamic law based on religious texts, to Catholic Church law and governance.

"Nobody is trying to push Sharia law on anyone else, just like I hope nobody is trying to push canon law on anybody else, because we live in an America where you should have the freedom of your religion," El-Sayed said.

TRUMP INAUGURATION PASTOR SAYS DEARBORN CHRISTIANS 'AFRAID' TO SPEAK OUT IN MUSLIM-MAJORITY CITY

The comparison sparked pushback on social media from users highlighting the differences between the two viewpoints and traditions.

"He lies and says no one is trying to push Sharia (they are), and draws a false equivalency to Christian Canon law," Andrew Kolvet, executive producer of "The Charlie Kirk Show," posted on X. "Canon law determines how Christian leaders, churches, and Christians should live, but Canon law is limited to affairs of the Church (spiritual penalties). Canon law grants great autonomy to the state."

Kolvet continued, "Sharia law is MUCH more comprehensive, governing all aspects of life, and historically, and according to many contemporary Islamic clerics, dictates the affairs of the state."

EL-SAYED'S AGENDA PUTS ‘PERMANENTLY’ CHANGED AMERICA ON THE LINE IN MICHIGAN SENATE RACE, GOP FIREBRAND WARNS

"Sharia law is incompatible with Western Civilization," political commentator Carl Jackson posted on X. "I’m tired of El-Sayed playing the victim card in attempt to avoid legitimate scrutiny of Islam."

"Yeah, it’s over for him," Fox News contributor Kaylee McGhee White posted on X. "Rogers by 6."

"@AbdulElSayed doesn’t get to bloviate about sharia being a mere ‘practice’ of faith when it’s Islamic jurisprudence used to supplant western jurisprudence," conservative commentator and radio host Dana Loesch posted on X.

"'Jesse, the Catholic Church requires ministers to use plant oils in sacraments with the blessings of a bishop, so why shouldn't courts allow Muslim men to have four wives?'" conservative commentator Michael Knowles posted on X.

"Canon law applies to Catholics," conservative commentator Pamela Geller posted on X. "There is no compulsion is Canon law. Jewish law applies only to Jews. There is no compulsion in Jewish law. It is voluntary. The sharia is a comprehensive legal system governing every aspect of human life, and asserts authority over non-Muslims."

"This was a very strange prepared defense from Abdul," GOP communicator Matt Whitlock posted on X. "I expected him to say it was out of context, not reflective of current views, etc. Instead he accepted the premise and defended promoting Sharia Law – opening that lane up to more attacks."

"Ultimately, the question is, when I die and I stand before God and go through everything I did in my life, I don’t want to say I did it the easy way instead of the Shariah-compliant way," El-Sayed told the Times.

You can’t understand the efforts to uproot Muslim Americans without understanding the Tulsa massacre. You cannot understand the challenges we face today without understanding White supremacy."

item.title: Angel Reese tainted a historic WNBA night with a shameless late-game stat-padding layup
item.description: Angel Reese's 26 rebounds broke the WNBA single-game record, but a controversial uncontested layup in the final seconds raised stat-padding questions.
item.content:encoded:
Angel Reese had a historic night Monday against the Los Angeles Sparks. She grabbed 26 rebounds in Atlanta's 78-71 win, breaking the WNBA single-game record (24) that Chamique Holdsclaw had held since 2003.

Her 20th rebound of the night also put her past A'ja Wilson for the most rebounds in a WNBA season.

Hitting the glass for 26 boards is an impressive record, no question (even if three of them were her patented "Mebounds"). But Reese and her Dream teammates tainted the historic night during the final 20 seconds.

ESPN TURNS ANGEL REESE’S 49 ‘MEBOUNDS’ INTO PROOF THAT SHE’S A LEGENDARY WNBA REBOUNDER

Atlanta led 76-69 with 20 seconds left and Reese had nine points. Following a Sparks possession that resulted in two missed shots, Dream guard Jordin Canada collected the rebound. It turns out that Reese never even attempted to play defense on the possession. Instead, she waited in the frontcourt for Atlanta to regain possession.

Canada did just that and then heaved the ball the length of the court to a wide-open Angel Reese with 15 seconds left.

Reese had the ball with a seven-point lead, and no defender near her. All she had to do was dribble out the clock and secure the victory. But if you've been paying attention to Reese's career, you can probably guess what happened next. Reese scored on an uncontested layup, giving her 11 points on the night and her 27th double-double of the season.

Atlanta didn't need the points. Reese needed them.

If an NBA player did that, there's a chance a physical altercation might follow. Instead, everyone simply accepted that Reese is going to do whatever she has to do to make sure the box score looks the way she wants it to look.

To be clear, Reese didn't find herself one unlucky bounce short of 10 points. She went 4-for-14 from the field and was 3-for-13 before the layup. The WNBA.com play-by-play lists seven missed layup attempts and all 10 of her missed shots came within 5 feet of the basket.

She also had five shots blocked and Sparks forward Cameron Brink blocked four of them.

Brink is the Sparks' only legitimate healthy rim-protector, and Los Angeles came into the game 13-24. Reese kept attacking her, kept getting turned away and then got the one layup nobody contested after the result had already been decided.

Her 26 rebounds were already in the books. The late basket didn't help her reach either rebounding record. It took her from nine points to 11, and it got her to double-double No. 27. Not only that, but Reese didn't get back on defense during a possession that could have mattered to ensure that she got her points.

ANGEL REESE 'DIDN'T SLEEP' AFTER BLOWING GAME-WINNING LAYUP AGAINST FEVER, SMIRKING CAITLIN CLARK

Reese is now one double-double behind Alyssa Thomas' WNBA single-season record of 28 and she has six games left to tie it. Given that she and her teammates seem intent on making sure she gets her numbers, Reese should be a lock to break that record. But should it come with an asterisk?

This isn't the first time a Reese double-double has needed help after the actual basketball part of the game was finished.

In 2024, her former team, Chicago, was closing out a win over her current team, Atlanta, when Reese needed one point to keep her double-double streak alive. She had seven points and 11 rebounds entering the fourth quarter, but struggled to score in the final frame, missing two layups over the first nine minutes. With 25 seconds left, she finally converted a layup to give the Sky a five-point lead.

It was a crucial bucket for the team, but left Reese one point away from the 10 she needed.

The Dream failed to score on their ensuing possession and the Sky hit two free throws after an intentional foul. Atlanta once again failed to score and was content to let the clock run out and end the game.

ANGEL REESE GOT A BARBIE DOLL, SIGNATURE SHOE AND WNBA THEME NIGHT, THEN PLAYED VICTIM AGAIN

Rather than just dribble out the rest of the clock, like almost every basketball team does in that situation, Chicago guard Chennedy Carter decided to get the ball to Reese, who had her arms in the air and was calling for Carter to pass her the ball.

Clearly, Reese knew she needed those points to get into double-figures and, despite the game being over, she wasn't going to pass up the opportunity to pad the stats and add to her record.

Reese was then fouled by an Atlanta defender, and she made both free throws to extend her double-double streak to 14 straight games.

Monday's layup came with a different team and a different record on the line. But the results were eerily similar. Reese knew the exact number of points she needed, put herself in a position to get those points despite the game being essentially over, and made sure her teammates did their part to help her.

A reporter opened a postgame question by congratulating Reese on the "NBA record," then immediately corrected himself.

"Well, you know what I'm talking about," he said.

"No, I don't cuz I be setting NBA records, too," Reese replied.

Look, the reporter obviously meant WNBA. Reese set WNBA rebounding records Monday night. She didn't set an NBA record because she plays in the WNBA, not the NBA.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Instead of laughing off the mistake and talking about her team's performance, she took the opening to brag about something that simply wasn't even true. Maybe she was joking, but it didn't sound like a joke.

It was an arrogant response to a reporter's verbal mistake, and it looks even worse after considering the stat-padding layup that she ended the game with.

Reese set two legitimate WNBA records on Monday. Then she cherry-picked two free points in a game Atlanta had already won because she just can't help herself.

item.title: Mamdani launches fast-track housing-court push, says landlords unable to comply ‘should not be a landlord’
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced New York City's Unified Court System will fast-track emergency housing court cases involving vacate orders and violations.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Tuesday the debut of the city's new Unified Court System, a mechanism to fast-track emergency cases in New York City Housing Court.

"I am proud to announce that the Unified Court System will now fast-track emergency housing court cases where the health, safety and well-being of New Yorkers is at risk," Mamdani said during a Tuesday news conference.

The new system will reduce the time tenants face to have emergency hearings on potential negligence from landlords, Mamdani explained.

"This fast track will accelerate the cases that are both the most egregious and the most complex. Cases where at least one third of units in a building are subject to an open vacate order. Where families have been forced from their homes. Cases where at least one third of the units have an open and immediately hazardous violation for essential services," he announced.

MANHATTAN BUILDING STABILIZED, SOME EVACUATIONS LIFTED AFTER COLLAPSE FEARED

In cases of "persistent and extreme negligence" where tenants request entirely new building management, judges will require parties to return to court "within five days after service is completed," Mamdani announced.

NYC RENT BOARD DISSENTER WARNS MAMDANI-BACKED FREEZE COULD HURT AFFORDABLE HOUSING OVER TIME: 'SLOW BURN'

When asked how his office would differentiate between a landlord who was persistently negligent and one who simply couldn't afford to keep up with the costs of building management, Mamdani did not hold back.

"We're talking about cases where a third of the building is facing some kind of a serious violation. Cases where we have elevators broken down," he started.

MAMDANI RIPPED OVER 'FREAK SHOW' NEWS CONFERENCE WHERE EVICTION WAS DECLARED A FORM OF 'VIOLENCE'

"When it comes to the law, everyone has to follow it. And for far too long that has somehow not been understood when it comes to housing in our city. If a landlord is not able to follow the law, then they should not be a landlord of that property," he replied.

When asked about how to enforce any violators who might not appear to Housing Court after the five-day window, Mamdani said, "There is still a lot of work to follow through on."

Fox News Digital contacted the mayor's office for further comment.

item.title: The 2026 NFL season hasn't even started yet and the Jacksonville Jaguars are already taking a massive L
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars' new NFL Rivalry uniforms feature spotted pants and clashing colors that are already catching serious heat from fans online.
item.content:encoded:
I tend to talk a lot about college football uniforms more than NFL uniforms, but that all changed Tuesday morning.

The NFL rolled out their "Rivalry" series of uniforms for all eight teams from the NFC North and AFC South, and by and large, they did a pretty nice job.

The league partnered with Nike to deliver some uniforms that feature a good bit of franchise history and community pride stitched into each team's garments, and I have to say I'm a fan of the overall concept.

CINCINNATI REDS DEBUT CITY CONNECT UNIFORMS AND THEY ARE AN ABOMINATION

I've always been a bigger fan of college uniforms and felt the NFL threads were a bit too "corporate" and "samey" for my liking, but almost all of these are sweet looking alternate kits.

All of them except for one team, that is.

JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS SET AT 8.5 WIN TOTAL AFTER SURPRISING 13-4 SEASON AND WILD CARD LOSS TO BUFFALO

The Jacksonville Jaguars, being an AFC South team, were included in the "Rivalry" uniform rollout, and if I'm being blunt, they massively swung and missed their intended target with these monstrosities.

Okay, let's start with the positives. At least they aren't the "Color Rush Thursday" mustard uniforms the Jags wore back in the late 2010s.

Well, that's about the only positive I can find, so let's dive in, shall we?

This is way too busy for my liking. The helmet, jersey and socks, and pants all being different colors is murder on my eyes. It looks like a 13-year-old kid customized Jacksonville's uniforms in Madden and picked the most garish combinations possible.

Why didn't they go with a black helmet like the good old days?

Or, if they wanted to do the teal lids, at least get a matching jersey and make the pants white.

And, oh Lord, the pants!

You might not be able to tell, but if you look closely enough on the graphic, those are indeed, spotted pants.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

You know, like a jaguar?

People like to rag on another team from the Sunshine State, the Florida Gators, for their "Gator Skin" jerseys, and rightly so. But these pants are just as egregious and deserve just as much flak.

And believe me, they are catching some heat from fans on social media.

The season hasn't even started yet, and the Jags are already taking L's all over the place.

On the bright side, if Trevor Lawrence throws for 400 yards and three touchdowns while wearing these and Jacksonville wins their division this year, everyone will look back fondly on these uniforms a few decades from now.

Time heals all wounds. Hell, just look at how popular the "Creamsicle" jerseys are in Tampa.

As Marty McFly would say, "I guess you aren't ready for that. But your kids are gonna love it."

item.title: NYC mom survives neck-slash attack on hiking trip in Arizona: 'I can’t die like this'
item.description: Ring camera footage captures New York City mother Alexis Rowan fighting for her life after a stranger slashed her neck on an Arizona birthday hike.
item.content:encoded:
A birthday hiking trip of a lifetime wound up being a death-defying fight for her life for a New York City mother of two, leaving her neck slashed, her hand stabbed, as well as physical and emotional scars that left 13 stitches and a nightmare that will never be forgotten.

Alexis Rowan, 27, survived the northern Arizona mountain-hike attack only because of screams that were heard by a woman in a nearby home, forcing the suspect to flee, harrowing doorbell camera footage showed.

"I was like, oh my God, my neck: I can't die like this, this is not the way," Alexis Rowan told WABC after returning to New York City after last week's ordeal on a tourist mountain hike in Arizona. "I have my kids to go home to."

NURSE IMPALED BY POLE DURING HIKE FORCED TO TREK 10 MILES FOR HELP: 'A FREAK THING'

Graphic photos shared by the New York Post showed the deep slash left on her neck and the 10 stitches that closed it, along with three more from being stabbed in the hand.

She never wants "to look at another mountain again," she told the Post, while the lasting scar will remind her of the horror with every look in the mirror.

On the Wednesday, Aug. 19, hike at the Havasupai Indian Reservation – just one day after her 27th birthday – Alexis was left briefly behind a friend when the suspect approached. The suspect, identified as Taylor Nardo Paya, 29, is a Havasupai tribe member with a rap sheet that included a guilty plea to assault, according to FOX 10 Phoenix.

GRIZZLY BEAR MAULS HIKER, DRAGS HIM DOZENS OF FEET ON GLACIER NATIONAL PARK TRAIL

"It was the first person that I've seen in the village, and I said, 'Hey, excuse me, is that the gift shop?'" Rowan told WABC in one of the few interviews she granted. Fox News Digital reached out to her and her mother for an interview, but they have yet to respond.

"I kept walking, I went to go in and that's when he just came up from behind," she continued, "and as soon as I felt my neck, I'm like, 'Oh my God, I'm going to die.'"

Footage showed Rowan fighting for her life as she was dragged by the hair from the ground – with her screams finally bringing a woman to open the door and causing the suspect to flee. The video obtained by Fox News Digital did not have the sound of the screams, but they were key to the suspect fleeing, according to reports.

REPEAT OFFENDER ACCUSED OF COLLEGE STUDENT’S MURDER WAS KNOWN ‘THREAT’ AFTER PRIOR ARREST: VICTIM’S MOM

"I'm just so grateful for the woman that opened the door that heard her screams; it's something you can never unhear," Tricia Rowan, Alexis' mother, told WABC of the "angel sent from heaven" woman who opened the door to help.

"She's a fighter. She fought to make sure she's coming home to her babies, and she's my baby. So I'm so glad she made it," Tricia Rowan said. "He picked the wrong one. My daughter is a fighter, she is a warrior. She wasn’t going to take it."

SENATOR TIM SHEEHY: SOFT-ON-CRIME JUDGES NEED CONSEQUENCES. THE JAIL ACT DELIVERS

Alexis Rowan told the Post she was "mentally aware" of the "danger" after her initial interaction with Paya.

"My gut instinct was like, ‘This is not OK. I’m not OK,’" she said, adding that the "next person may not be as strong, may not be prepared mentally that someone is going to attack them or able to put them in danger."

Reservation police located Paya the following day by pinging Rowan’s phone, which prosecutors say he allegedly stole after it fell from one of her backpacks.

WOMAN ALLEGEDLY CHOKED SUBWAY RIDER, YELLED ANTISEMITIC REMARKS IN ATTACK CAUGHT ON VIDEO: POLICE

He was arrested and later taken into federal custody because the alleged attack occurred on tribal land, according to reports. Video obtained by Fox News Digital showed Paya being cuffed and taken away on a golf cart by federal police before another video showed him in an orange jumpsuit being perp-walked to a helicopter.

Paya faces a federal assault with a deadly weapon charge, according to FOX 10. Court records show Paya pleaded guilty in 2016 to robbing and assaulting another woman in a 2015 attack, for which he received a five-year prison sentence and was ordered to undergo sex offender treatment and counseling.

The victim's mother wants to see the perpetrator locked up indefinitely.

"People are evil," she told the Post, calling him "a threat to society" and someone "you cannot rehabilitate."

"There is no place on earth that they belong," she added, "other than behind bars like an animal in a cage because they’re predators and they prey on innocent victims."

item.title: Mystery trio in headlamps and overalls emerges from Manhattan manhole, prompting NYPD probe
item.description: The NYPD is reviewing surveillance video after three people in overalls and headlamps were caught emerging from a Manhattan manhole near Penn Station.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Police Department is investigating after video showing three people in overalls and headlamps emerging from a Manhattan manhole went viral on social media.

The NYPD confirmed to Fox News Digital that the incident occurred on Aug. 18 at 4:19 a.m. on the southeast corner of 32nd Street and Seventh Avenue, which is near Penn Station.

No arrests have been made in this case, but police said they are reviewing surveillance video.

NYPD detectives told WABC that they believe many of the people who have been caught on camera doing this are migrants searching for valuables in the sewers.

WOMAN DIES AFTER PLUNGING INTO UNCOVERED MANHOLE OUTSIDE LUXURY STORES

Detectives said a scavenger culture exists in nations like Venezuela.

City officials have said that sneaking into manholes is both illegal and "extremely dangerous."

NYPD INVESTIGATING AFTER SURVEILLANCE VIDEO CAPTURES GROUP ENTERING SEWERS THROUGH MANHOLES

"DEP has inspected the sewers at the location, and our infrastructure is safe. DEP works closely with our public safety partners to help ensure the safety and security of critical infrastructure throughout New York City," the city's Department of Environmental Protection said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

The statement continued: "Entering the sewer system is both illegal and extremely dangerous. Sewers can contain numerous hazards, including noxious and potentially deadly gases, unstable surfaces, flooding risks, and confined spaces. For these reasons, members of the public should never enter a pipe, drain, catch basin, manhole, or outfall."

New York City's sewer system is made up of an elaborate network of more than 7,400 miles of wastewater and stormwater pipes, parts of which date back to the 1800s.

In June, The Associated Press reported on three separate instances of people exiting manholes in Queens and the Williamsburg and Gravesend neighborhoods of Brooklyn.

Many of them were wearing headlamps and were carrying shovels or other tools when they were caught on video.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Antisemitic streamer finally makes Dem leader snap with rare rebuke: ‘Malicious’
item.description: House Minority Leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries calls Hasan Piker's claim that Jewish Americans invite violence against themselves dangerous and antisemitic.
item.content:encoded:
House Minority Leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York is slamming comments from Hasan Piker after the far-left controversial online streamer suggested that Jewish Americans were inviting violence against themselves over their support for Israel.

"The malicious claim that American Jews are inviting violence against themselves is dangerous and antisemitic," Jeffries charged in a social media post. And he added in a CNN interview on Tuesday that Piker's comments were "malicious" and "should not be tolerated by anyone in the public square."

While Jeffries became the highest-ranking congressional Democrat to fire back at Piker, the criticism from the top Democrat in the U.S. House comes after he has largely stayed silent on the far-left insurgency, backed in part by Piker, that's gripped his party this election cycle.

Jeffries spoke out after Piker, on his stream last week, featured an image of state Sen. Jeremy Moss, the Democratic nominee in Michigan's 11th Congressional District. Moss, who is Jewish, has said that people are sharing a fake audio clip of him claiming that his entire reason for running for Congress is to make sure that America continues to support Israel.

EL-SAYED TRIES TO DISTANCE HIMSELF FROM HASAN PIKER AFTER LATEST FIRESTORM

"If Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they are singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone is going to come around and take action, not against the state of Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker warned.

Piker, who has over three million online followers, has repeatedly stood by his numerous past comments slamming Israel over its ongoing war against Hamas in Gaza.

Jeffries emphasized in his social media post, "There is zero justification for threats against the safety of our Jewish brothers and sisters at a moment of rising hate. We will fight the cancer of antisemitism with the fierce urgency of now."

ABDUL EL-SAYED FACES OFF WTIH FOX NEWS' JESSE WATTERS IN PRIMETIME

Piker's comments were also blasted by Democratic Rep. Hillary Scholten, D-Mich., who charged that Piker is "a hack who thrives on hate."

Rep. Susie Lee, D-Nev., took to X to write, "Claims that American Jews are responsible for the violence being committed against their communities are unacceptable and cannot be tolerated. It’s dangerous and antisemitic."

"We must stand up to the scourge of antisemitism wherever it rears its ugly head," Lee added.

Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., praised Jeffries' pushback against Piker.

In an interview on Fox News' "America's Newsroom," Gottheimer called Piker's comments something "right out of the Nazi playbook."

Gottheimer, who is Jewish and a strong supporter of Israel, emphasized, "This is a call for violence against Jews,"

He was also critical of Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan.

DEMOCRATS 'WHO NEVER VOTED REPUBLICAN' BACKING THIS GOP SENATE NOMINEE

El-Sayed, who is facing off against former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in battleground Michigan in a high-stakes Senate showdown, on Monday tried to put some distance between himself and Piker, who is a top supporter.

"I want to be crystal clear, nobody speaks for this campaign besides me and my campaign spokespeople," El-Sayed said in a statement.

Gottheimer said that El-Sayed insufficiently pushed back against Piker: "El-Sayed's response was pathetic,"

"No Democratic members should allow Piker anywhere near them on the campaign trail," Gottheimer argued.

Piker endorsed El-Sayed for the Democratic nomination and appeared at some of the candidate's campaign events including a primary night party earlier this month in Detroit, Michigan.

Piker's latest comments were blasted by a growing number of Republicans since they grabbed attention this past weekend, including Rogers, who took aim at both Piker and El-Sayed in a social media post.

"More calls for violence coming out of the El-Sayed campaign," Rogers said on Sunday. And he claimed, "Here is his running mate, Hasan Piker, saying that if AMERICAN JEWS support Israel, they will be violently targeted because of it."

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Rogers, who is making a major push to court Democrats in Michigan, added, "Absolutely DISGUSTING. If Abdul El-Sayed had any courage at all, he would call this out and disavow Hasan Piker once and for all. We’re waiting, Abdul…"

El-Sayed, in his Monday statement, wrote, "I believe all Americans deserve the right to advocate for what they believe without fear of violence. This is particularly true for communities that have been intimidated for their beliefs in the past."

"My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters. Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk," he added.

WHAT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS IN THE MIDTERM RACES SHOW

A former Wayne County Health Department director, El-Sayed, if elected in November, would make history as the nation's first Muslim senator. The epidemiologist who unsuccessfully ran for governor as an insurgent candidate in 2018 has made support for Medicare for all a major component of his campaign and has also called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

El-Sayed used the word "bloodthirsty" to characterize Israel's military moves in Gaza in an MS NOW interview this month and accused Israeli leadership of genocide against Palestinians. He has argued against unconditional U.S. military aid to Israel, as have other progressive politicians. And El-Sayed has repeatedly declined to directly answer whether Israel has the right to exist.

But El-Sayed has also repeatedly stated that he stands "in solidarity with my Jewish sisters and brothers" to "condemn antisemitism."

item.title: Former TOPGUN pilot analyzes Marine Corps pilot's eerie calm after emergency F-18 ejection
item.description: Former TOPGUN pilot Matthew Buckley explains the violent forces of ejection and why Marine Corps Maj. Jackson Simon appeared so calm after his F-18 crash.
item.content:encoded:
Former TOPGUN pilot Matthew "Whiz" Buckley told Fox News Digital that the recent crash of a Marine Corps F-18 in Washington state — and the pilot's split-second decision to eject — highlights both the violence of the maneuver and how the ensuing shock can leave an aviator feeling eerily calm.

On June 13, 2026, Marine Corps Maj. Jackson Simon emerged from a wooded area with a bloodied face and walked down the road toward a Yakima County sheriff’s deputy, whose bodycam captured the pilot appearing remarkably composed.

"I'm a little frazzled," was about as close as Simon came to expressing fear after his F-18 Hornet crashed into the forest and sparked a small wildfire near Rimrock Lake.

Buckley, who flew F-18 Hornets during his 15-year career in the U.S. Navy, said Simon was likely experiencing a combination of shock, an adrenaline letdown and the effects of training that teaches pilots to compartmentalize under pressure.

EIGHT BELIEVED DEAD AFTER B-52 CRASHES SHORTLY AFTER TAKEOFF FROM EDWARDS AIR FORCE BASE

"If anything's going wrong, we focus on the task. Everything else goes away," Buckley told Fox News Digital. "That was the most violent thing that ever happened to that Marine in his entire life."

Buckley served as a pilot in the Navy from 1991 to 2006 and said he was fortunate never to have ejected from an aircraft. The experience can have a devastating toll on the human body.

"Some folks don't go back to flying status. I mean, you can lose a couple inches in height. Your spine compresses. Some people get shorter," Buckley said.

A meta-analysis of more than a dozen studies looking at 1,710 military aircrew ejections found a pooled mortality rate of 10.5%, while 29.8% suffered major injuries. The studies were published between 1971 and 2019.

ARMY IDENTIFIES 2 PILOTS KILLED IN APACHE HELICOPTER CRASH NEAR FORT HOOD DURING TRAINING EXERCISE

"When you pull that handle, you have two choices: die or maybe live. And I said 'maybe live' because it's incredibly violent. I think the average ejection seat is like 10 to 20 G's of force," Buckley added. "Most folks don't even remember the ejection. They remember pulling the handle and then waking up in their parachute."

Buckley said the pilot's body positioning before the ejection is extremely important in preventing potentially life-threatening injuries. For example, if their arm is extended away from their body, the sudden wind blast could cause it to be "ripped out of the socket."

There's also a phenomenon called "seat slap," which occurs if the pilot does not have their legs flush with the seat prior to ejecting.

"If you look at an ejection seat in a fighter jet, it's rock hard. We're not sitting on a cushion," he said. "If your legs aren't flat on the seat, it could break both of your legs and now you bleed out and die."

US NAVY IDENTIFIES SAILOR LOST IN ARABIAN SEA AFTER HELICOPTER'S EMERGENCY WATER LANDING

In some instances, pilots who find themselves in trouble have time to slow their aircraft and perform a controlled ejection, which can reduce the forces involved, Buckley said.

Based on video of the crash, Simon’s plane was traveling at a high rate of speed before it struck the trees and exploded, likely leaving little opportunity for a controlled ejection.

Simon had been performing low-flying maneuvers while spectators on the ground watched, according to KIRO 7. After that, his plane reportedly clipped some power lines, which led to it going down.

The Marine Corps has not publicly confirmed that Simon’s F-18 struck power lines before the crash and has said the cause of the mishap remains under investigation.

UNITED AIRLINES JET FLEW TOO LOW AND TOO SLOW BEFORE STRIKING LIGHT POLE AND TRUCK NEAR NEWARK AIRPORT: NTSB

According to Buckley, this "clearly" wasn't supposed to happen.

"We have minimum altitude restrictions. And there ain't no 500-foot trees, right? So I don't know what they were doing. It doesn't sound like from his initial statement that there was anything wrong with the airplane. So that's usually not a good sign," Buckley said.

Buckley then speculated about what may have been going through Simon’s mind before the crash.

"It looked like a beautiful day. People out on a lake. 'Hey, there's some people down there on the lake. Why don't we go show them what their tax money is [for]? You know, America.' I hope it wasn't something like that," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the third Marine Aircraft Wing, the West Coast-based Marine aviation unit to which Simon’s aircraft was assigned.

Buckley said Simon will likely go before a review board that will evaluate his actions surrounding the crash. At the conclusion of the process, the board can recommend what should happen to an aviator’s flight status.

If he's found to be at fault, Simon could lose his "wings" or he could be allowed to continue flying, just under what Buckley described as "double secret probation."

"I don't know what the board's gonna do, but it'll come out. It should because...this is a $60 to $65 million Hornet. We deserve to know what happened," he added.

item.title: New Padres owner Kwanza Jones puts on a performance for the ages at introductory presser
item.description: Kwanza Jones broke into a spirited chant about winning it all during her introduction as a new San Diego Padres owner after the $3.9 billion sale.
item.content:encoded:
As a singer and songwriter, Kwanza Jones knows a thing or two about putting on a performance, and she made sure to show off those abilities as she was introduced as a new owner of the San Diego Padres.

Jones, along with her husband, Jose E. Feliciano, took over ownership of the Padres in a $3.9 billion sale from John Seidler and his family earlier this month. The pair were introduced to the media in San Diego on Monday, and it's safe to assume that Jones is rather excited about the new, incredibly expensive endeavor in Major League Baseball.

"We gonna win. We gonna win. We’re going to win, win it all," Jones shouted while offering up some hand gestures as well. "We hope it’s sooner rather than later."

SAN DIEGO PADRES STAR MANNY MACHADO IS WRONG TO COMPLAIN ABOUT MODERN MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL

Jones also stood up at one point during the news conference and took a picture of the gathered media with her phone.

Padres fans are hopeful that sooner rather than later part comes to fruition, especially considering that they've been waiting forever to see San Diego win a World Series.

The Padres have played in the World Series twice in franchise history, most recently in 1998, but have never hoisted the Commissioner's Trophy.

PRIVATE EQUITY COMPANY APOLLO AGREES TO FINANCE DEAL WITH NEW YORK YANKEES ORGANIZATION FOR $2.6 BILLION

Feliciano is an investor and the co-founder and managing partner of the investment firm called Clearlake Capital, the 12th largest private equity firm in the world. Forbes reports that his net worth is $3.9 billion.

Feliciano is not new to the sports owner's world, as Clearlake co-led a group of investors in an acquisition of Chelsea in the Premier League in May 2022.

Jones and Feliciano could be in store to witness postseason baseball in San Diego this year, with the Padres currently holding onto the third Wild Card spot in the National League with a record of 71-61.

The Padres currently hold a two-game lead over the Arizona Diamondbacks in the Wild Card race with 30 regular-season games to go.

item.title: Formula 1 champ Max Verstappen set to take on 100 go-karters in wild made-for-TV stunt
item.description: Max Verstappen will race against 100 go-karters on a purpose-built track at Silverstone in a made-for-TV event airing on ESPN and on Disney+.
item.content:encoded:
If you've ever wondered what it would be like to turn one of the best Formula 1 drivers of all-time loose on a karting track with 100 mere mortals, we're going to find out.

It was announced that Red Bull's four-time champion Max Verstappen — fresh off a rough weekend in which he crashed out of his home race on the opening lap — will take on scores of karters in a special, made-for-TV event called "Max vs 100."

It will take place on a purpose-built karting track at Silverstone — site of the British Grand Prix — and will be broadcast on ESPN and streamed on Disney+.

This will be wild.

First of all, I'm a sucker for made-for-TV stunts. Motorcycle jumps, tightrope walks, whatever David Blaine feels like doing (which is usually hanging upside down or sitting in a chunk of ice for a few days), I'm in.

EVEL KNIEVEL'S MOST LEGENDARY STUNTS RETOLD IN EXCLUSIVE NEW FOX NATION DOCUMENTARY

While this doesn't have the danger factor of Evel Knievel sending it over the fountain at Caesars Palace, it will be a display of just how good the Dutchman is behind the wheel of anything.

I don't think it's a matter of whether Max Verstappen can overtake go-karters; it's how long it will take him to do it.

Like most F1 drivers, Verstappen started his racing career on karts, so he'll have to reach into his old bag of tricks.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

"In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking," he said in a statement, per Motorsport. "Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it's always nice to return. It’s about understanding the grip of the go-kart. I've done so many years in go-karting that you quite naturally get back into things."

I'm curious to see how hard the karters defend against him. On one hand, it would be cool to say you made it hard for a driver of Verstappen's caliber to get past you, but you don't want to be the guy who causes a crash by moving under braking or not leaving enough space through a corner.

Don't. Be. That. Guy.

item.title: ICE lodges detainer for illegal immigrant with lengthy rap sheet after alleged jealousy-fueled killing
item.description: ON FOX: Federal immigration officials lodged an ice detainer for a Cuban citizen with drug trafficking convictions charged with second-degree murder.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Federal immigration officials are asking authorities in the Miami area to honor a detainer request for an illegal immigrant with a lengthy criminal history who is now charged with fatally shooting a man on the street in an alleged act of jealousy.

William Serrano Domenech, 49, is being held in a Miami-Dade County jail in connection with the Aug. 17 murder of 42-year-old Raul Aballe, the Department of Homeland Security said Tuesday.

"He has a rap sheet a mile long, with prior convictions in Florida and Michigan for drug trafficking and illegal possession of a firearm, as well as prior arrests in New Mexico and Tennessee for aggravated assault, theft, and resisting arrest," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "This dangerous criminal should have never been in our country, and had it not been for the Biden Administration releasing him from ICE custody in 2023, Raul Aballe would still be alive."

EXCLUSIVE: DHS SEEKS CUSTODY OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER TRUMP DEPORTATION, BIDEN RELEASE

Domenech, a Cuban citizen, was "socializing with the witness" on the evening of the slaying when Aballe appeared and the pair began arguing, authorities said. The dispute turned physical when Domenech started punching and slapping Aballe, authorities said.

Domenech allegedly pulled a gun out of a fanny pack and opened fire, striking Aballe in the stomach. Aballe was taken to a hospital where he later died.

ICE LODGES DETAINER ON SALVADORAN NATIONAL, 18, ACCUSED OF 2 FATAL SHOOTINGS IN HOUSTON

Domenech allegedly fled the scene, but he was arrested the next day. He allegedly admitted to the killing and said he was jealous of Aballe's relationship with the witness, according to authorities.

The witness reportedly told investigators that Aballe was not armed and didn't initiate the fight.

HOW A NONCITIZEN SUSPECTED KILLER GOT CAUGHT AND RELEASED BY NEWSOM-APPOINTED JUDGE: TIMELINE

Domenech is charged with second-degree murder and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) lodged a detainer with Miami-Dade authorities the day after Domenech's arrest.

His criminal history spans at least four states for a litany of offenses, DHS said. That includes a conviction for a weapons offense and arrests on charges of vehicle theft, burglary, driving without a license, and driving with a suspended license in Florida, as well as prior arrests on charges of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, false imprisonment, and bribery of a witness in New Mexico.

HUNDREDS OF JAILED ILLEGAL ALIENS RELEASED BACK ONTO BLUE-STATE STREETS DESPITE ICE DETAINERS, RECORDS SHOW

In addition, Domenech has prior arrests for unlawful possession of a weapon, resisting arrest, and theft in Tennessee, and convictions for possession with intent to distribute five grams or more of cocaine, possession with intent to distribute an unknown quantity of marijuana, possession of firearms in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime, possession of a firearm by an illegal alien, and felon in possession of a firearm in Michigan, authorities said.

Domenech allegedly told authorities he entered the United States through Florida in 1995. A deportation order was issued by a judge in 2002.

ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CHARGED WITH BRUTAL SLAYING ONE DAY AFTER CALIFORNIA JUDGE RELEASED HIM: DHS

However, when ICE took him into custody in 2023, he was released back onto the streets by the Biden administration, DHS said.

"ICE has lodged a detainer and will work with our partners in Florida to ensure that this killer is never again allowed back onto our streets," Mullin said.

item.title: Georgia sheriff seizes 1,800 pounds of suspected black-market marijuana shipped from California
item.description: A 1,800-pound black market marijuana shipment from Sacramento, California, was intercepted in Georgia, reportedly bound for Atlanta and Orlando.
item.content:encoded:
A massive shipment of 1,800 pounds of suspected black-market marijuana from California was intercepted in Georgia on Tuesday, with authorities saying the drugs were destined for Atlanta and Orlando.

The shipment originated in Sacramento, where recreational marijuana is legal, according to the Butts County Sheriff’s Office. Sheriff Gary Long said about half of the marijuana was bound for Atlanta, while the rest was headed to Orlando.

The sheriff’s office did not say where or how the shipment was intercepted, whether anyone was arrested or whether charges were filed.

NY TIMES WALKS BACK STANCE ON MARIJUANA LEGALIZATION, ADMITS LOOSENING OF POLICIES HAS MADE COUNTRY WORSE OFF

Long used the seizure to make his case that legalizing marijuana does not eliminate illegal sales.

"But here is the reality: the black market isn't going away," Long said in a press release announcing the seizure.

Marijuana laws vary among the three states connected to the shipment. California allows recreational marijuana, while Georgia and Florida allow marijuana only for certain medical uses.

"The illegal marijuana trade does not stop at the state line," Long said.

Long said Mexican drug-trafficking organizations and other criminal groups continue to move large amounts of marijuana across state lines. The sheriff’s office did not say the shipment seized Tuesday was connected to a cartel or any other criminal organization.

The sheriff also argued that illegal sellers can undercut licensed marijuana businesses because they don't pay taxes or licensing fees or have to follow testing and other regulatory requirements.

"As long as there is demand and money to be made, illegal dealers will continue to operate," Long said.

AMERICA HITS MAJOR MARIJUANA MILESTONE AS DAILY WEED USE SURPASSES DAILY DRINKING

Long urged Georgia lawmakers to look closely at what has happened in states that have legalized marijuana before making changes to Georgia's laws.

He pointed to California, which has changed its cannabis tax and regulatory system while continuing to fight illegal marijuana sales. He also cited past ballot initiatives filed in Colorado seeking to repeal constitutional provisions that legalized recreational marijuana, though those efforts did not reverse legalization.

"That should be a warning to Georgia," Long said. "We should learn from the experiences of states that have already gone down this road instead of repeating the same mistakes and then spending years trying to fix them."

Long said his statement was not meant to settle the question of whether marijuana should be legal. Instead, he argued that lawmakers need to consider how illegal sales and trafficking would fit into any changes to Georgia law.

"Georgia, let's get it right the first time," Long said.

item.title: Google Docs password leak reveals a costly security mistake
item.description: A contractor stored credentials in a Google Doc set to "Anyone with the link," and Google Search autocomplete eventually surfaced the password string.
item.content:encoded:
Passwords have a way of ending up in places they were never meant to live. Sometimes convenience wins in the moment, and security becomes tomorrow's problem. One company learned that lesson after a contractor stored credentials in a Google Doc so they could access them from different devices.

Then something happened that should make anyone who uses Google Docs take a closer look at their sharing settings. A developer searching the company's domain on Google saw one of its staging hostnames appear in autocomplete alongside what looked like a credential string. The company investigated and found a Google Docs URL that anyone with the link could access.

That's a rough way to discover that a password has traveled much farther than you intended. Here's how the exposure happened, what Google says about Docs privacy and the simple steps you can take to keep your own passwords and shared files safer.
